doctrine.text: Protecting your rank has a real cost. Price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template players are the default owns. Passing on them needs a priced case.

Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice. Sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline. Brighton beat Arsenal 3-0 on 19 September and Coventry beat Forest. Both are one result. The Arsenal defenders hold, and Dasilva is on the list with a trigger, which is what this rule is for.
A cheap-defender haul only tells you about one match. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week. Then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used. It is also the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up. Ignore the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position. Two of the room's bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro. None owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

An open window changes who plays before it changes who you should buy. Buy after the window shuts. It paid on 1 September. Two of the five went to bed owning an Everton midfielder and woke up owning a Manchester City substitute, and nobody who waited lost anything by waiting.

A cup tie tells you about the team sheet more than the result. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything. That is why a 35-year-old's header, a flagged striker's replacement and a vice-captain's absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night. It held again on Wednesday. Chelsea made nine changes, went 2-0 down, and the four men who came on at half-time won it 6-3. The scoreline says Chelsea are fine. The team sheet says the fringe is a long way from the eleven. It held a third time on 15 and 16 September. White, Mosquera and Hincapié were missing from Arsenal's cup squad, Shaw from United's, and Kinsky and Van de Ven sat on the Spurs bench. All of that is Saturday's team news.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need 90 minutes. Deadline day settled six calls here without a ball being kicked. They were the Liverpool winger, the Arsenal forward, the United left-back, the Everton striker, the Everton midfielder and the City left-back. A trigger only a scoreline can fire sits open through the weeks that decide the player.

A room that agrees has no protection against being wrong together. Not one of the five captained Haaland this week. The three who did in GW1 all moved off him. He scored twice at Palace before any of their captains had kicked a ball. Check what the room has agreed on, not only what it argues about. A week later all five captained him against Coventry. The room moves together in both directions. He scored against Coventry and all five got 18. Agreement was right this time and it gave nobody an edge. GW4 made it three weeks running. Three of the five captained Haaland and scored within 1 point of each other. The two who moved off him lost 8 and 14 to the armband, and so did Ted's side. GW5 made it four weeks running, and this time all five captained him. Sir Fergie moved off Palmer and The Special One off Isak to do it. Sunday decides whether it cost anyone. Sunday settled it. Haaland scored once for 12 and all five got the same, so the armband decided nothing between them. The two moves onto him both paid, Sir Fergie's off Palmer and The Special One's off Isak.

Grade a rule by what it cost. Do not grade it by how sensible it sounded. D5 declined the £4.0m Hull defenders after one haul because they were flagged and it was one match. Two weeks on Hull have six points, two clean sheets, and the two best-scoring £4.0m defenders in the game. A rule that only ever says no stops being useful. Three weeks on it is three clean sheets, and D5 is retired.

A Bench Boost wants 15 players who start. It does not need a double gameweek. The page called Sir Fergie's chip premature on Saturday. By Sunday night every one of his 15 had played, and it had won him the week and the lead. Grade a chip by the team sheet it lands on. The calendar does not matter.

A player sold inside the league has not gone, he has just moved clubs. The price on his card does not move for a week either. Ndiaye is worth £6.0m in two of these squads this morning and is fourth in the queue at his new club. Read the new shirt, forget the old fee.

Do not grade a player on 45 minutes. Three sacks were reversed on Wednesday. They were a winger hooked at half-time, a defender who came on as a substitute, and a left-back who was never actually dropped. It happened again on Thursday. The Hull back four sacked on Monday for six deadline-day arrivals turns out to be the back four the head coach intends to keep. Wait for the second data point when the first one is a substitution. It held a third time on Sunday. The winger hooked at half-time at Villa Park started at the Emirates, played all 90 and got a 7 from the BBC. Cherki was taken off at half-time in the derby and goes down anyway, because Foden's ban changes the shirt and the second data point is the Sunderland team sheet. It held a fourth time on 20 September. Cherki, hooked at half-time in the derby and downgraded anyway, started against Sunderland and scored.

The injury flag moves last, after the news is already out. Arsenal's centre-back missed Thursday's open training with Chelsea to come and carries no flag in the player file. The £75m midfielder beside him missed it too. A squad that is picked on Friday afternoon is reported on Thursday night and flagged on Saturday morning. Read the training ground first, then the file. It held on Saturday morning: the flag arrived two days after the training report, at 75%. It held a third time this week. Gakpo missed the Atlético game on Wednesday and the 75% flag arrived on Thursday. It held a fourth time this week. João Pedro missed Tuesday's training, withdrew from Brazil's squad on Wednesday, and the flag arrived at 75% with no diagnosis. It held a fifth time on Friday. ESPN had the scan result, a ligament sprain and 3.5 weeks, while the file sat at 75% and the manager said "a possibility". It held a sixth time on Friday. João Pedro missed Brentford as ESPN said he would, and the file has him at 75% on Saturday morning.

A verdict of squad depth needs a team sheet. Ndiaye was sacked on Monday as fourth in the queue at City and started his first game there on Saturday. D15 said read the new shirt. The page wrote the verdict before the shirt existed.

The bench is where this room loses points. Le Professeur left 25 there and The Special One 17, and both did it the week before. Read your own bench before reading the transfer market. This week the bench order is the whole decision. All five own João Pedro, Chelsea kick off after the deadline, and the first sub is the man who plays if he does not. The auto-sub also has to keep a legal formation. A gaffer starting five midfielders cannot have a sixth come on for a striker, whatever the bench order says. On Friday the room read its own bench. Le Professeur sold Tzolis, so Groß can now come on for João Pedro. Sir Fergie moved Vuskovic to the bench as the cover. Mr CR7 bought Groß as the cover. The Special One benched João Pedro and started Gvardiol. On Saturday both owners of Groß left him on the bench and he scored 14, the top score in the room for a second week. Mr CR7 and Le Professeur get it back through the auto-sub because João Pedro did not play. Sir Fergie's bench has 19 on it and Thomas, the man he sacked in his head, is 9 of it. GW5 closed with Thomas's 9 on Sir Fergie's bench and Verbruggen's 6 on Le Professeur's, behind Kinsky's 2.

A Free Hit on a single gameweek buys one weekend and returns the same squad on the Monday. Xabi played his in GW5 with Elanga, Shaw and João Pedro in the squad and no free transfer spent. It scored 48, second of the five for the week, and 14 of it was Tarkowski, who leaves on 10 October. The same three men come back that day with the same problems. Grade the chip against what the old eleven would have scored, and against the transfers he did not make.

A starter in a side that scores three a game blanks because somebody else scored. Sack him on minutes or on price. Semenyo was sacked on one assist in four league games and scored 17 against Sunderland. Wirtz was sacked on 12 points in four and returned at Bournemouth. Both started every game in between.

Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.

Saturday of a gameweek one fixture old. Upgraded Cherki to nailed on the start his trigger asked for, plus two goals at Selhurst Park, and recorded that not one of the five captained Haaland before he scored twice. Moved Guéhi back towards a buy once Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back. Settled Watkins on the £50m Al-Hilal sale and Martinez on Villa confirming the Chelsea deal. Opened Foden, O'Reilly, Diouf, Delap and Muñoz. Recommended no transfer again, on the grounds that the window shuts on Tuesday and the GW3 deadline is the Friday after it — the first week of the season in which waiting costs nothing. Minted D12 on the armband.

Saturday's five fixtures settled four open triggers and opened a hole. Upgraded Tarkowski to solid on the late goal at Bournemouth, exactly the trigger written on Thursday. Sacked Tonali, whose trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle and who was substituted in a 2-0 defeat, and sacked Gravenberch, who was left out of the pivot rather than keeping a clean sheet in it. Moved Igor Jesus back to watch after he started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, and cooled Delap for the same reason. Cooled Kerkez after he was taken off on 71 minutes, and cooled Woltemade after Wissa scored at Spurs and Napoli were reported to want him on loan. Settled Sánchez and Muñoz by transfer. Opened Isak, Gibbs-White, Elanga, Wissa, Scott and the three Hull picks. Minted D13 against the brain's own D5: the £4.0m Hull defenders it declined after one haul now have two clean sheets behind them and thirty-six points between them. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday.

Gameweek 2 settled everything except Villa v Arsenal. Marked the brain's own Bench Boost rule under review after Sir Fergie played one in a single gameweek and won the week and the lead with it — D14. Upgraded B.Fernandes on a hat-trick that fired his blank trigger the other way, and upgraded Maguire, Lammens, Schade, Calvert-Lewin, Wissa, Ajayi and Tzolakis. Sacked Lacroix on the exact trigger written on Thursday — a clean sheet against a depleted Brighton — after Chelsea conceded three and reached eighteen games without one. Sacked Caicedo, who came off in tears after eleven minutes, Kerkez a week early on the substitution rather than the missed start, Welbeck on an unused bench at 4-3, and Woltemade once Wissa started and scored. Cooled Ndiaye with Spurs in advanced talks, Semenyo on one assist at £8.5m, De Cuyper on an advanced role that is not the position he was bought for, and Havertz on Arsenal chasing Álvarez. Opened Rashford, Neto and Groß. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday, with the deadline three days behind it.

First run with the window shut. Recommended the room's first transfers of the season. Ndiaye out for Mr CR7 and Le Professeur after his £65m move to Manchester City, and Aït-Nouri out for The Special One on City calling him third-choice left-back. Reversed three sacks that deadline day settled the other way. Gakpo stays after Liverpool rejected £80m. Shaw keeps his place after United failed to sign a left-back. Barry becomes Everton's only striker after the Balogun deal collapsed. Sacked Tzolis on a 4/10 and a half-time substitution, and Konsa on coming off the bench rather than starting. Cooled Cherki, Foden and Semenyo on City signing two more attackers, and cooled the whole Hull back four on six deadline-day arrivals and the sale of a defender who had played all three games. Promoted D9 to doctrine on the evidence it just produced, retired D6 into D14, and minted D15 on players sold inside the league.

Deadline eve. Reversed three of Monday's own sacks after reading the window post-mortems. Tzolis was graded on 45 minutes, but impressed in the Community Shield and on the opening day. Konsa was signed because Saliba and Timber are injured, and the man ahead of him limped off. Kerkez stays because Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola knows him from Bournemouth. Upgraded Gvardiol to nailed on City saying O'Reilly moves into midfield, which reverses last week's trigger. Downgraded Szoboszlai on Liverpool naming him as right-back cover, and Gakpo on Barcola's likely debut at Ipswich. Upgraded Ajayi on the flag coming off. Recommended captaincy calls rather than transfers for three of the five, and minted D16. A verdict written on 45 minutes proves nothing.

Deadline day, window shut. Read the training ground rather than the player file. Mosquera and Bruno Guimarães both missed Arsenal's open session on Thursday. Downgraded Mosquera without a flag, moved Konsa and White up, and told Le Professeur to promote Konsa off his bench rather than spend a transfer. Reversed Monday's cooling of the Hull back four after Jakirovic said the six deadline-day arrivals must earn shirts, and put Ajayi back on the house list. Opened Barcola, Guéhi and Bruno G., and sacked Richarlison outright. He was left out of Spurs' registered Premier League squad. Upgraded Verbruggen on Rodon's eight-to-ten-week hamstring and Leeds improvising at centre-back. Repeated the Ndiaye transfer for the two owners and the Aït-Nouri sale for The Special One. Minted D17. The flag moves last.

Saturday, one fixture into GW3. Friday night at Ipswich settled three of Thursday's triggers the right way. Kerkez kept the clean sheet his trigger asked for, Gakpo made both goals with Barcola on the bench, and Szoboszlai played in midfield while Araujo debuted at right-back. Upgraded all three to solid and opened Isak, Jacquet and Araujo. Read the deadline. All five captained Haaland and The Special One played his Wildcard from last place with 12 changes. Mr CR7 sold Ndiaye and started Calvert-Lewin as recommended. Le Professeur sold Konsa the day before every predicted Arsenal XI named him. Downgraded Shaw on a hamstring fitness test, Hume on a predicted Sunderland XI without him, and Dewsbury-Hall on Grealish's return. Downgraded Mosquera again as the flag arrived on Saturday morning, two days after the training report, which is D17 holding once. Rewrote the Team radar for the Saturday and Sunday team sheets. No transfer recommended. The GW4 deadline is a week away and Sunday's derby decides four Arsenal and Chelsea calls.

Saturday of GW3, one match in. Friday night settled three Liverpool triggers the right way. Gakpo started and made both goals while Barcola came off the bench, so Gakpo goes up to solid. Kerkez kept the clean sheet his trigger asked for and goes up. Szoboszlai played in midfield with Araujo on debut at right-back and goes up. Opened Isak, Jacquet, Araujo, Wirtz, Frimpong, Diop, Dedić, Egan, Raya, Mainoo and Delap. Downgraded Mosquera again once the 75% flag arrived, two days after the training report, which is D17 holding. Noted that all five captained Haaland a week after none did, and added it to D12. Read the Newcastle team sheet: Hornicek in goal, Hall and Elanga starting, Fernandez-Pardo on the bench. Recorded The Special One's Wildcard at 16 points after one match, with Raya on the bench behind Tzolakis, and Le Professeur selling Konsa the day before Mosquera was flagged. Set the GW4 question for the whole room as the derby captaincy. No roast: the gameweek is live.

Sunday of GW3, seven fixtures played. Saturday settled a dozen triggers. Cherki went up to solid on a second start, Guéhi on a return to centre-back, Kinsky on Spurs' first clean sheet, and E.Le Fée on the penalty at Brentford. Hume went to sack once Danso made his debut. Ndiaye came back from sack to watch after starting at the Etihad five days after both owners sold him, and D18 records the miss. Semenyo's trigger asked for a goal and he produced the assist, so he holds at watch. Verbruggen's clean-sheet trigger did not fire. Opened O'Reilly on the warm-up injury, Enzo Fernández and Foden on the City team sheet, Mendy, Ballard, Van de Ven, N.Williams, Suzuki, Mitchell, Scott, Tavernier, King, Bogle and Barnes. Retired D5 on Hull's third clean sheet. Rewrote the Team radar for Porto, the cup ties and the derby week. No transfer recommended before Sunday's two games.

Monday, GW3 played and the bonus settling. Sunday settled the Arsenal and Chelsea triggers. Konsa started and made the team of the week, so he goes up to solid and Mosquera, out with a muscle problem, goes to sack. Tzolis started 90 and goes up, and Eze, who did not get on, goes down. Ødegaard and Havertz scored and both go to nailed. Rogers scored after two minutes for a goal or assist in all three Chelsea games and goes to nailed. Palmer was booked and kept quiet and holds. Mbeumo scored again and goes up. Lammens conceded twice for the third game running and goes down. Mainoo goes up on another start. Opened Šeško on a goal off the bench, Rashford on the knock, Cunha on the false nine role, James on midfield, George and Maitland-Niles on the Everton goals. Cooled Dewsbury-Hall with Grealish back. Rewrote the Team radar for the Champions League week and the derby. Told Le Professeur his bench of Kinsky, Rogers and Cash outscored three starters. No transfer recommended before Tuesday's team sheets.

Tuesday, GW3 finished and the bonus in. Settled the GW3 log. Monday 2 September is a miss: Ndiaye was sold as squad depth and started, and two of the three sacks were reversed within a day. Wednesday, Thursday, both Saturday entries and Sunday are hits, with Gakpo the one downgrade that went the wrong way. Monday's entry stays open because its calls are for the derby. Ted's first 15 scored 78, which beat all five. Wrote the rebuild note only, with the GW4 draft opening this evening. Caicedo, Mosquera and O'Reilly all moved to 75% in the file overnight. Sánchez went to Como, so Martinez is Chelsea's one goalkeeper. Woltemade went to Juventus, so Wissa is Newcastle's one striker and goes up. Read Maresca on resting Haaland before Porto. Villa replace Spurs on the radar. No transfer recommended before the midweek team sheets, and the derby captaincy stays the room's question.

Thursday, the GW4 draft open and the derby deadline on Saturday. Read the midweek team sheets. Shaw was rested against Sabah after cramp and did not train on Wednesday, so he goes down to watch. Maguire went to the bench behind Yoro and goes down. Šeško made his first start and goes up. Gakpo missed Atlético and the flag arrived a day later, which is D17 holding again. Barcola and Araujo go up on the starts they got. Calafiori was rested at Napoli and holds. Konsa started again, White goes up on the pass that made the winner. Palmer scored twice off the bench and goes up. Opened Welbeck, Neto, Estêvão, Mac Allister, Muharemović, Janelt, N.Jackson and McGinn. Haaland scored twice at Porto and played the full game. Ted's GW4 squad is written. Isak captain over Haaland, B.Fernandes left out, Palmer and Ødegaard in, Kinsky in goal. The room's question is the derby captaincy and the two calls that changed this week are Shaw for Xabi and Gakpo for The Special One. No transfer recommended for a hit.

Tuesday, GW4 played and the bonus settling. Settled the GW4 log. Thursday is a miss: Ted captained Isak over Haaland and got 4 against 18, Maguire went down and started, White went up and limped off at half-time. Monday and Tuesday are hits. Read the weekend. Elanga is out long-term and goes to sack, and both owners are told to sell. Shaw was left out of the derby squad and goes to sack. Foden is banned until 17 October. Cherki goes down to watch after a half-time hook, Szoboszlai and Kerkez go down on the Fulham game, Wirtz and Semenyo to sack. Raya, Gabriel, Guéhi, Jacquet, Groß, Schade, Kinsky, Tarkowski and Calvert-Lewin go up to nailed. Martinez and Lacroix go to sack on the Hull goals. Opened Donnarumma, Belloumi, Bogle, Emersonn, Davis, Kostoulas, Igor Jesus, Evanilson, Mykolenko, Solanke and Thomas. Told Le Professeur that Groß scored 17 on his bench and The Special One that Gvardiol scored 11 on his. Told Xabi and Mr CR7 to replace Elanga before Friday. Minted D19 on benches. Ted is live and untouched.

Thursday, the GW5 draft open and the deadline on Friday night, with Chelsea kicking off after it. Read the cup team sheets. João Pedro withdrew from Brazil's squad and missed training, so he goes down to watch and the bench order becomes the room's decision. Welbeck opened at watch. White missed Arsenal's cup squad and goes to sack, Konsa moves up with the shirt his. Shaw missed United's cup squad and holds at sack. Gakpo started and scored in the cup and goes up to solid. De Cuyper scored the winner at Old Trafford and goes up to nailed. E.Le Fée scored his penalty and goes up, Hume started in Europe and comes off sack, Ballard goes down with Alderete starting. N.Jackson goes to sack behind Abraham. Promoted D10 to pattern on the third cup week that told the team news. Ted's GW5 squad is written. Haaland captain, Palmer vice, João Pedro left out, Saka and Schade in, Trafford in goal. Told Xabi and Mr CR7 their first subs are Shaw and Elanga. Told The Special One to start Gvardiol for White. No transfer for a hit recommended.

Friday, deadline day for GW5, six hours out. Read the scan. ESPN reports João Pedro has a ligament sprain and 3.5 weeks of recovery, while Alonso called Friday a possibility and the file stayed at 75%. That is D17 a fifth time. He holds at watch because the break covers the recovery. Corrected Thursday's advice to Le Professeur. Groß cannot come on for João Pedro in a side with five midfielders, so the auto-sub would bring on Cash. Told him to start Groß and Diop himself. Told Xabi to buy Schade for Elanga and start him, Mr CR7 to buy Davis for Shaw and Schade for Elanga, Sir Fergie and The Special One that the free transfer buys Calvert-Lewin. Read Thursday night. Haaland rested, Cherki off at half-time again with the tie won, Bournemouth and Palace both played in Europe before weekend fixtures. Read Friday. Arteta says White, Mosquera and Timber are fine and Tuchel left White out of England with a groin injury. Mosquera up to watch, Mendy and Dedić confirmed out. England recalled Palmer, Calvert-Lewin, Konsa, Guéhi, Hall, O'Reilly and Mainoo. Ted's 15 stands as drafted on Thursday, Haaland captain and João Pedro out. Added the formation rule to D19.

Saturday, GW5 one match in. Read Friday night. Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0, João Pedro missed it as ESPN said, and the file sat at 75%, which is D17 a sixth time. Palmer holds at nailed on the BBC's best Chelsea rating and 2 points. Rogers goes down to solid on his first blank and a finish up front. Welbeck goes to sack on 17 touches. Caicedo and James go down after missing the squad. Martinez and Lacroix hold at sack on a third goal conceded. Schade holds at nailed on two assists, Ajer goes up on the clean sheet his trigger asked for, M.Sangaré goes to sack off the bench. Opened Thiago, Anthony, Schuster, Kelleher, Kayode, Colwill and Murillo. Read the deadline. Xabi played the Free Hit and captained Haaland. Sir Fergie and The Special One moved the armband to Haaland, so all five captain him. Le Professeur sold B.Fernandes and Tzolis for Saka and Palmer at a cost of 4, and the sale makes Groß a legal sub for João Pedro. Mr CR7 sold Elanga, Shaw and E.Le Fée for Belloumi, Groß and Konsa at a cost of 4. The Special One sold White for Murillo. Rewrote the Team radar for the weekend team sheets and 10 October. Minted D20 on the Free Hit. Ted is live and untouched.

Sunday, GW5 six matches in and four to play. Read Saturday. Brighton beat Arsenal 3-0, so Raya goes down to solid on the trigger, Ødegaard goes down on two blanks, and Calafiori, Gabriel and Konsa hold on one match. Eze goes to sack with no league start before the break. Groß holds at nailed on 14 from two benches, Kostoulas goes up to solid on a second goal, Verbruggen up to nailed on the clean sheet, Yalcouyé down to watch on a bench. Kinsky goes down to solid on three conceded, N.Jackson comes off sack on the start and the goal, McGinn goes up. Tarkowski holds at nailed on 14, Barry and Mykolenko go up, Pickford opens at solid. Hall and Barnes go up, Wissa goes to sack on the saved penalty, Tzolakis goes down to watch on two conceded, Willock opens. Thomas goes up on Coventry's first clean sheet, Dasilva and Rushworth open at watch. Told Sir Fergie, Mr CR7 and Le Professeur that Vuskovic, Groß and Groß come on for João Pedro when the gameweek closes. Told The Special One his 19 is second so far with six to play. Rewrote the Team radar for the four Sunday games and 10 October. Ted is live and untouched.

Thursday, GW5 settled and the squads sit until 10 October. Settled the GW5 log. Tuesday is a miss, with Semenyo sacked before scoring 17 and Cherki downgraded before scoring. Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday are hits, and Ted's 15 scored 66, which beat all five again. Read Sunday. Shaw started at Fulham and comes off sack, Cunha goes up on the goal, B.Fernandes and Mbeumo go down on blanks, Šeško and Rashford go to sack on the shin and the England withdrawal. Semenyo, Enzo and Cherki go up on the Sunderland goals. Guéhi, Donnarumma and O'Reilly go down on three conceded and a bench. Kerkez goes up on the start and the clean sheet, Wirtz on the assist, and Szoboszlai holds one blank from a sack. Bogle goes to nailed. Trafford, Virgil, Brobbey and Rice open. Palmer goes down to solid on the England withdrawal. Told Xabi the Wildcard is the 10 October question, Mr CR7 that B.Fernandes is one blank from a sell, and Le Professeur to start Verbruggen. Minted D21 on sacking starters in sides that score three a game. Wrote Ted's rebuild note only.

Friday, first week of the break, the squads locked until 10 October. Read Thursday night in Amsterdam. Havertz went off after 30 minutes for Germany holding his hamstring and goes down to watch, with Gyökeres up to watch behind him. Brobbey lasted 35 minutes for the Netherlands and has left the squad, so he goes to sack four days after the hat-trick, and Isidor opens at watch. Both flags arrived in the file overnight. Palmer holds at solid with Chelsea calling the withdrawal load management. Told the Brighton owners that Sunderland may be without their striker on 10 October. No change to the five, no transfer recommended, and Ted's rebuild stands.

why.name: Palmer
why.text: Sir Fergie is the one of you who owns him, and he wears the vice armband here. ESPN says João Pedro is out for 3.5 weeks, so Palmer takes the penalties and the central shirt at Brentford. England recalled him on Friday. 26 points at £9.7m.

why.name: Saka
why.text: None of you own him. 30 points at £9.5m, the penalty at Sunderland, and he was rested for the cup at Ipswich. Brighton have scored 10 in four and conceded in three of them, so Arsenal will get chances.

why.name: Schade
why.text: None of you own him. Two goals at Bournemouth and 30 points at £6.1m. Chelsea on Friday night have conceded two in every league game, and may arrive without their striker.

why.name: Groß
why.text: Le Professeur owns him and benched him for 17. Brighton's penalty taker at £5.7m, and Hürzeler says Dunk and Vuskovic are both fit behind him. Arsenal at home is the hard fixture. He stays in for the set pieces.

why.name: Guéhi
why.text: None of you own him. A clean sheet in the derby beside Dias and 26 points at £6.0m. Sunderland at home is the softest fixture on the ticker, and Sunderland scored once against Arsenal.

why.name: Gvardiol
why.text: Mr CR7 starts him and The Special One benched him for 11. The cross that made Haaland's derby goal, a clean sheet, and Sunderland at home. Maresca says Doku is out for Sunderland, so the left side is his this weekend.

why.name: Bogle
why.text: None of you own him. 37 points at £4.6m, the best-scoring defender in the game, with a goal against Newcastle. Palace at home on Sunday, and Palace played Thursday night with Sarr and Nketiah only fit for the bench.

why.name: Trafford
why.text: None of you own him. A clean sheet against Newcastle behind a Leeds side with one defeat in 13 league games. £5.0m, and Palace come to Elland Road with Mateta out and 48 hours after a European tie.

why.name: Mykolenko
why.text: None of you own him. A clean sheet at Spurs for 11 and 22 points at £4.5m. Ipswich at home, and he is first off the bench if any of the back three is a late doubt.

why.name: Davis
why.text: None of you own him. A goal and an assist at Selhurst Park, 23 points at £4.0m, and he plays every week. Everton away is the week he sits.

why.name: Emersonn
why.text: None of you own him. 24 points at £5.5m and a goal at Selhurst Park. He is the third forward and the cover if Calvert-Lewin is a late doubt.

why.name: Steele
why.text: None of you own him and he does not play in the league. He is the £4.0m that lets Saka and Palmer both start. A ghost with no transfers needs no second keeper.

left_out.name: João Pedro
left_out.text: All five of you own him. ESPN says he has fluid in the knee from a ligament sprain, 3.5 weeks of recovery, and misses Brentford. Alonso called Friday "a possibility" and would not rule him out. Chelsea kick off after the deadline. Calvert-Lewin takes the £6.0m and Palace at home.

watchlist.name: Gibbs-White
watchlist.note: None of you own him. 26 points at £8.0m, the penalties, and Coventry at home, who have lost five of six and have Awoniyi banned. He is out because Saka is in, and a blank from Saka swaps them.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: None of you own him. 29 points at £6.1m and Ipswich at home. Mykolenko keeps the same clean sheet for £1.6m less, which is why he sits on the bench and Tarkowski sits here.

watchlist.name: Šeško
watchlist.note: None of you own him. Two starts in a week now, both in cups. A league start at Fulham and a goal puts him in at £7.0m for the run after the break.

ted.rebuild: The 15 scored 66, which beat all five of you again. Groß, Trafford and Schade carried it with 33 between them, and Haaland's late goal doubled to 12. Palmer, Saka, Rogers and Calvert-Lewin cost £32.9m and returned 8, and Mykolenko kept a clean sheet on the bench behind three defenders who all played. The GW6 draft opens on 6 October.
